the front's composition from the north: a canted bay with two lights a storey, the door's column over a straight stoop, then the corner block's two lights a storey, round-headed in the principal storey

the corner block's mansard stands about a storey higher than the rest in the photograph (its dormers' heads at y 230-330 px against the north bay's at y 330-400); the build carried the whole mansard at one height. the north bay rises under its own curved mansard with two dormers in the photograph (its crown's top about y 300-330 px of the box, its two lit dormer lights at x 300 and 395 px, square-headed under a dark cap, over the bay's pair of lights); T-3283 carries the bay up through the cornice under a mansard of its own, the house's moulded stone cornice carried round its three faces, its lower faces 3.0 m at 80 degrees to a curb about level with the house's, and its two dormers on its front face 0.6 m either side of its middle, gabled as the house's are; the two dormers that stood on the house's mansard behind it are gone. the camera sees the 20th Street flank more openly than the render (the flank's bay at x 1050-1200 px of the box); the eye is held at a chosen stand (26.6 px RMS) and the flank's depth of view is not fitted; and the front's north half is drawn narrower than the photograph's: the north bay's lights and the door both stand about 55-60 px south of the photograph's while the corner block's lights land on theirs, so the door's column agrees with the picture relative to the bay and the gap is the camera's, not the door's (T-3283) [T-3283, 2026-11-02: a camera fit, not a difference in the house. The halftone cannot fix the eye (the solve's own words: good for which element stands where, not for a dimension read off it alone), so this is the gap two camera fits disagree about, T-3153's within tolerance.]
